section_name: Introduction: Welcome to Python — Your Gateway to Big Tech
description: Set up a fully working Python development environment, understand the Python ecosystem, write and run your first Python script.

lessons.title: Core Concepts: Python Ecosystem
lessons.html_content:
Python is the #1 language at Google, Netflix, Amazon, Instagram & Spotify — for web, ML, automation, and cloud.

Key Concepts

  • What is Python? Interpreted, high-level, dynamically typed
  • Python 3.x — always use Python 3.11 or higher
  • The ecosystem: pip, virtual environments, standard library
  • How Amazon uses Python: AWS Lambda, boto3, data pipelines
  • Running Python: terminal scripts, Jupyter notebooks, cloud functions

Your First Script

print("Hello, World!")
import sys
print(f"Running Python {sys.version}")
name = input("What is your name? ")
print(f"Welcome to Python, {name}!")

lessons.title: Coding Practice: Setup Verification
lessons.html_content:
Exercise 1: Setup Verification

Run python --version in your terminal. Then write a script that prints your version using import sys and print(sys.version).

Exercise 2: Personal Intro Script

Write a script that asks for your name, age, and dream company with input(), then prints a formatted welcome message using an f-string.

Exercise 3: Explore pip

Run pip list in your terminal and write a Python script that prints a welcome message listing 3 Python libraries you want to learn.

lessons.title: Reference Readings
lessons.html_content:
Recommended Reading

  1. Python Official Tutorial — docs.python.org — The authoritative beginner reference.
  2. How Amazon Uses Python (AWS Blog) — aws.amazon.com — Real-world Python usage at Amazon scale.
  3. Real Python: First Steps — realpython.com — Well-structured intro with interactive examples.

assignment.title: Dev Environment Showcase (Amazon Theme)
assignment.instructions:
Every Amazon engineer starts Day 1 by setting up their environment exactly right. Prove yours is production-ready.

Tasks:
1. Screenshot of python --version showing Python 3.x
2. A script setup_check.py that prints your Python version, OS name, and 5 installed packages
3. A short reflection (100 words): Why Python? What do you want to build?

forum.title: Introduction Discussion
forum.prompt: Think of a problem in your daily life that repeats. How could a Python script automate or simplify it? Describe the problem in 150–200 words and explain what your script would do. Reply to 2 peers and suggest one Python feature they could use.
